d: The LangChain 1.0 function for building a tool-calling agent loop, configurable with middleware.
c:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
agent = create_agent(model="openai:gpt-5.5", tools=[search], system_prompt="Be helpful.")
x: create_agent replaces langgraph.prebuilt.create_react_agent as the recommended agent API.

d: Pluggable hooks that intercept the agent loop before/after model calls, around tool calls, and at start/end.
x: Middleware is passed to create_agent through the middleware= list.

d: Middleware hook that runs before each model call, e.g. to trim or inspect messages.
x: before_model runs before every model call in the agent loop, not just once.

d: Middleware hook that wraps each model call, able to modify the request, retry, or swap the model.
x: A wrap_model_call middleware receives the request and a handler to call the model.

d: Middleware hook that wraps each tool execution, useful for retries, logging or blocking calls.
x: wrap_tool_call runs around tool executions rather than model calls.

d: Built-in middleware that summarizes older messages when a token or message threshold is reached.
x: SummarizationMiddleware can trigger on token count and keep the most recent messages.

d: Built-in middleware that pauses before selected tool calls so a human can approve, edit or reject them.
x: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware requires a checkpointer so the run can pause and resume.

d: Built-in middleware that detects and redacts, masks or blocks personal data such as emails.
x: PIIMiddleware can redact emails from user input before the model sees them.

d: Built-in middleware that caps the number of model calls in a run or thread.
x: ModelCallLimitMiddleware(run_limit=10) stops a run after ten model calls.

d: Decorator for middleware that computes the system prompt at runtime from state or context.
x: A @dynamic_prompt function returns the system prompt string to use for the call.

d: create_agent argument that makes the agent return a validated structured object in structured_response.
x: create_agent(..., response_format=Ticket) puts the result in result["structured_response"].

d: Package containing LangChain's base abstractions: messages, prompts, runnables, tools, parsers and interfaces.
x: Provider integrations depend on langchain-core abstractions.

d: Package holding legacy v0.x chains and agents such as LLMChain and RetrievalQA after the v1 cleanup.
x: In LangChain v1, legacy chains like RetrievalQA moved to langchain-classic.

d: Separate packages such as langchain-openai and langchain-anthropic that implement models for each provider.
x: ChatAnthropic lives in the langchain-anthropic package.

d: The October 2025 major release focused on agents with create_agent, middleware and standard content blocks.
x: LangChain and LangGraph both reached 1.0 in October 2025.

d: Helper that creates a chat model for any provider from a "provider:model" string.
c:
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
model = init_chat_model("openai:gpt-5.5", temperature=0)
x: init_chat_model("anthropic:claude-sonnet-5") returns an Anthropic chat model.

d: The message type returned by chat models, carrying content, tool_calls and usage metadata.
x: AIMessage.usage_metadata reports input and output token counts when the provider returns them.

d: Standardized, provider-agnostic view of message content such as text, reasoning, images and tool calls.
x: content_blocks normalizes content across providers in LangChain v1.

d: Message type that carries a tool's result back to the model, linked by tool_call_id.
x: A ToolMessage must reference the id of the tool call it answers.

d: Message type holding instructions that set the model's behaviour for the conversation.
x: A SystemMessage is typically placed first in the message list.

d: Runnable method that yields output chunks as they are generated.
c:
for chunk in model.stream("Write a haiku"):
    print(chunk.content, end="")
x: model.stream(...) yields AIMessageChunk objects.

d: Runnable method that runs many inputs, in parallel where possible, returning outputs in input order.
x: runnable.batch([a, b]) returns a list of outputs in the same order as the inputs.

d: Runnable method that tries alternative runnables when the primary one raises an error.
x: with_fallbacks only uses the fallback when the primary runnable raises an exception.

d: Runnable method that automatically retries a failing call a configured number of times.
x: with_retry(stop_after_attempt=3) retries up to three attempts.

d: A rate limiter you attach to chat models to cap requests per second.
x: A rate_limiter can be passed when constructing a chat model.

d: String template with {variables} that formats into a single prompt string.
c:
pt = PromptTemplate.from_template("Summarize in {n} words: {text}")
pt.format(n=10, text="...")
x: PromptTemplate.from_template("Hi {name}").input_variables is ['name'].

d: Template that formats variables into a list of role-tagged chat messages.
x: ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages accepts (role, template) tuples.

d: Prompt element that inserts a list of messages, such as chat history, at a position in the template.
x: MessagesPlaceholder("history") expects a list of messages under the key history.

d: Prompt method that pre-fills some template variables, returning a new template.
x: prompt.partial(date="2026-11-21") leaves the remaining variables to fill later.

d: Writing {{ and }} in f-string style templates to produce literal braces.
x: To show a literal JSON brace in a PromptTemplate, write {{ or }}.

d: Template that renders example input/output pairs as chat messages for few-shot prompting.
x: Few-shot templates take a list of examples and an example_prompt.

d: The LangChain Expression Language, which composes runnables with the | operator into chains.
x: In prompt | model | parser, the output of each step becomes the input of the next.

d: The common interface (invoke, batch, stream and async variants) implemented by prompts, models, parsers and retrievers.
x: Retrievers implement the Runnable interface, so they can be piped in LCEL.

d: Wraps a plain Python function so it can be used as a runnable in a chain.
x: (RunnableLambda(lambda x: x + 1) | RunnableLambda(lambda x: x * 2)).invoke(3) returns 8.

d: Runs several runnables on the same input concurrently and returns a dict of their outputs.
x: RunnableParallel(a=r1, b=r2).invoke(x) returns {"a": ..., "b": ...}.

d: Runnable that returns its input unchanged, often used to forward the question in a RAG chain.
x: RunnablePassthrough().invoke("x") returns "x".

d: Keeps all input keys and adds new keys computed from the input.
x: RunnablePassthrough.assign(n=lambda d: len(d["text"])) on {"text": "abc"} returns {"text": "abc", "n": 3}.

d: A dict literal inside a chain is automatically converted into a RunnableParallel.
x: Writing {"a": r1, "b": r2} | prompt creates a parallel step feeding the prompt.

d: Async method that streams fine-grained events such as token chunks and tool starts from a runnable.
c:
async for ev in chain.astream_events(inputs, version="v2"):
    print(ev["event"])
x: astream_events lets a UI show intermediate steps, not just the final output.

d: Output parser that extracts the text content of a model message as a plain string.
x: StrOutputParser().invoke(AIMessage(content="hi")) returns "hi".

d: Chat model method that returns validated objects matching a Pydantic model, TypedDict or JSON schema.
x: with_structured_output uses native tool calling or JSON-schema features of the provider.

d: Option of with_structured_output that returns the raw message and parsing errors along with the parsed object.
x: include_raw=True helps debug cases where parsing the model output fails.

d: Parser that adds format instructions to the prompt and parses the model's text into a Pydantic model.
x: parser.get_format_instructions() produces text you insert into the prompt.

d: Parser that turns model text into JSON and can stream partial JSON objects.
x: JsonOutputParser can emit partially parsed JSON while streaming.

d: Turns a typed, documented Python function into a tool whose docstring becomes its description.
x: The tool's argument schema is derived from the function's type hints.

d: Chat model method that tells the model which tools it may call, returning a model that can emit tool_calls.
c:
model_with_tools = model.bind_tools([get_weather])
ai = model_with_tools.invoke("Weather in Pune?")
ai.tool_calls
x: After bind_tools, the model returns tool calls; your code still executes the tools.

d: List on an AIMessage of the tools the model wants to run, each with name, args and id.
x: Each entry in tool_calls has a name, an args dict and an id.

d: Option that forces or restricts which tool the model must call.
x: tool_choice="any" forces the model to call at least one tool.

d: Injected parameter giving tools access to agent state, context, store and stream writer.
x: Tools can read runtime context such as a user id through ToolRuntime.

d: Integration that converts tools from Model Context Protocol servers into LangChain tools.
x: MultiServerMCPClient can connect to stdio and streamable HTTP MCP servers.

d: LangChain's unit of loaded text with page_content and a metadata dict.
x: Loaders return a list of Document objects with page_content and metadata.

d: Component that reads a source (PDF, web page, Notion, database) into Document objects.
x: PyPDFLoader produces one Document per page with the page number in metadata.

d: The default text splitter that tries separators in order (paragraphs, lines, spaces, characters) to keep text coherent.
x: chunk_overlap repeats text between neighbouring chunks to preserve context.

d: Splitter that chunks Markdown by headers and stores the header path in metadata.
x: MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter keeps section headings as metadata on each chunk.

d: Standard interface with embed_documents and embed_query that converts text into vectors.
x: Embeddings expose embed_query for queries and embed_documents for lists of texts.

d: A simple vector store kept in Python memory, useful for tests and prototypes.
x: InMemoryVectorStore loses its data when the process exits.

d: Vector store method that returns a Runnable retriever with configurable search type and k.
x: as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 4}) returns the top four documents.

d: Maximal marginal relevance retrieval that balances relevance with diversity among returned documents.
x: MMR fetches fetch_k candidates and selects k that are relevant but diverse.

d: Exposing retrieval as a tool so the agent decides when and how often to search.
x: Wrapping a retriever in a @tool lets create_agent call it multiple times per question.

d: Persistence component that saves conversation state per thread so agents remember earlier turns.
x: Passing the same thread_id in config lets the agent resume prior state.

d: Configuration key that identifies a conversation so its checkpointed state can be loaded.
x: Two different thread_id values keep conversations isolated.

d: A store such as InMemoryStore or PostgresStore holding facts across threads, organized by namespaces.
x: Stores persist information across threads, unlike thread-scoped checkpoints.

d: Streaming mode that yields LLM token chunks with metadata as they are generated.
c:
for token, meta in agent.stream(inputs, stream_mode="messages"):
    print(token.content, end="")
x: stream_mode="messages" is used to show tokens live in a UI.

d: Streaming mode that yields the state changes produced by each step (model or tools).
c:
for chunk in agent.stream(inputs, stream_mode="updates"):
    print(chunk)
x: updates mode emits one chunk per step showing what changed.

d: Observability enabled by environment variables that records every run's inputs, outputs, latency and tokens.
x: Setting LANGSMITH_TRACING=true and an API key enables automatic tracing.

d: The deepagents harness built on LangChain/LangGraph that adds planning, a file system and sub-agents.
x: deepagents is built on top of LangChain and LangGraph.
